carla: Heads up — after flipping paged-attn to FlashV2 in the dedicated cluster I see a p99 tail regression ~25% on long sequences (8k). Repro command I used: `./bench/paged_attn --model=gpt2 --seq=8192 --threads=8`. Anyone else hit this?
sam: Can you paste the perf run or a flamegraph? link + rough numbers will help.
carla: gist: https://gist.redwood/perf/flashv2-8192 (private) — top of nvprof output pasted below. Note the large time in the KV page walk kernel: 
```
nvprof summary:
gpu__flashv2_forward       0.42%   1.23ms
gpu__kv_page_walk         34.9% 103.2ms
gpu__flashv2_backward    0.39%   1.10ms
```
amanda: 34.9% on `gpu__kv_page_walk` is alarming. FlashV2 added tile prefetch changes — could be touching pages in a different order and causing more work. Is this only on the dedicated pool or reproduces locally? :thinking:
carla: Only reproducible on dedicated nodes (rtx-dedicated-*). I ran a local single-gpu quick test and the regression is ~5% (noise). On the 8-GPU dedicated pool it's visible and stable.
ryan: Can you try toggling `--kv-prefetch`? FlashV2 exposes a prefetch path that we enabled by default. Also try `--batching=legacy` to see if batching heuristics interact.
carla: Quick results: `--kv-prefetch=false` brings p99 down ~12% (so halfway back to v1), `--batching=legacy` changes tail shape but doesn't fully recover. So prefetch looks implicated but not the whole story.
sam: Any changes in kernel launch patterns? small kernels more often vs few big kernels? that affects PCIe/driver scheduling and page walk overlap.
carla: I captured an abbreviated trace:
```
TIMELINE:
launch kernel A (flashv2_tile_prefetch) -> cudaMemcpyAsync -> kernel B (kv_page_walk) -> small memcpy -> kernel C (dot)
Observed: more interleaved small memcpys when prefetch on.
```
amanda: Hypothesis: FlashV2's prefetch issues the page-walk kernel earlier for many small tiles causing hotspotting in the block table and extra TLB churn. If the pager on those nodes uses a slightly different eviction policy we could see this amplify.
infra-bot: deployed canary runtime `runtime-2026-03-15T10:22` to pool gpu-dedicated-blue for testing.
ryan: Next tests to run (assigning):
- sam: add counters for page_faults and outstanding_io to the paged-attn profiler (low effort)
- carla: run mixed-load microbench (80% short, 20% long seq) with prefetch on/off and upload logs
- amanda: bisect FlashV2 PRs that touched prefetch / kernel ordering
sam: I'll add a small instrumentation patch to surface kernel queue depth and per-kernel enqueue timestamps. If we see a bursty pattern that matches the pagewalk spikes we'll have more evidence.
carla: Also flagging this as a canary hold until we understand it. For now I recommend defaulting `--kv-prefetch=false` for paged-attn in canary runtime.
ryan: Agreed. After instrumentation we can iterate: if it's a kernel ordering problem we may inject a micro-batching barrier to coalesce page-walks. If it's TLB/page-table thrash we might add a light-weight pre-touch or change the allocator stride.
amanda: One more note — saw a small increase in host-side CPU syscalls in the logs when prefetch enabled (~+30% sys time). Could be pager thread activity. Capture `pidstat -w` and `perf record -e minor-faults` on the host next run.
carla: Will do and post results. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:
